bug_description.original: OSS-Fuzz issue 42534993 (boringssl): Use-of-uninitialized-value found by fuzz target ssl_ctx_api [msan]. https://issues.oss-fuzz.com/issues/42534993
bug_description.normalized: The `ssl_ctx_api` fuzzer reads a u8-length-prefixed operand into `std::string profiles` and passes `profiles.c_str()` to `SSL_CTX_set_srtp_profiles`. `ssl_ctx_make_profiles` then parses that operand with `strchr` as a colon-delimited C string, and the staged 25-byte witness makes `strchr` consume a trailing byte that MSAN traces back to the heap allocation underlying the `std::string` assignment.

source.description: First project-code read on the vulnerable path. `GetString` consumes the next byte from the remaining `CBS` as an 8-bit length and aliases that many attacker-controlled bytes as `str`, creating the exact field that later becomes the SRTP profile string.
source.value_from: The staged `poc` is exactly 25 bytes: `e7 17` followed by twenty-three `20` bytes. In `LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput`, selector byte `0xe7` dispatches to `kAPIs[231 % 48]`, the SRTP-setting lambda at `fuzz/ssl_ctx_api.cc:452-457`, leaving 24 bytes in `cbs`. This step then consumes length byte `0x17` and aliases the remaining 23 bytes, all ASCII spaces with no `:`.

relation.description: Source identity relation for the vulnerability-relevant value.

sink.description: MSAN sink. `ssl_ctx_make_profiles` treats the caller-supplied buffer as a C string and asks `strchr` to scan from `ptr` until `:` or `\0`. For the witnessed 23-space payload there is no colon, so `strchr` reaches the trailing byte at offset 23, which MSAN reports as uninitialized.
sink.note: The staged sanitizer trace says `Uninitialized bytes in strchr at offset 23 inside [0x7030000005a0, 24)` and reports the crash at `ssl/d1_srtp.cc:174:11`.

root_cause.description: This call discards the explicit `CBS_len(&str)` bound and hands the operand to a parser that only understands NUL-terminated, colon-delimited C strings. On the witnessed path the payload is 23 spaces with no colon, so the downstream parser can terminate only when it reaches the string's trailing sentinel byte.
root_cause.note: The saved `patch.diff` and declared `fixed_commit` do not touch `fuzz/ssl_ctx_api.cc` or `ssl/d1_srtp.cc`; this root-cause statement is grounded in the vulnerable source and MSAN evidence rather than patch corroboration.

parser_admitted.description: The first PoC byte is `0xe7`, so `index % 48 == 39` and the fuzzer dispatches into the SRTP lambda at lines 452-457. That admits the remaining 24 bytes to the exact vulnerable helper path.

tainted_value_origin.description: This `std::string::assign` call copies the 23-byte attacker-controlled payload into heap-backed string storage. MSAN attributes the later poisoned byte to the heap allocation performed underneath this assignment (`std::__1::basic_string<...>::__assign_external`).

fine_trace.note: Reads the length-prefixed string operand from the remaining `CBS`. On the witnessed path, this succeeds with `CBS_len(&str) == 23` and `CBS_data(&str)` pointing to 23 attacker-controlled space bytes; `GetString` is reached because the earlier selector byte `0xe7` routed the fuzzer to the SRTP lambda.

Copies the 23-byte payload into heap-backed `std::string profiles`. Every copied byte is `0x20`, so the string data contain no `:` and any later delimiter search must continue to the trailing byte. MSAN's origin chain attributes the later poisoned byte to the heap allocation performed inside this assignment.

The guard returns only if `GetString` fails; on the witnessed path it succeeds, so the lambda hands `profiles.c_str()` to `SSL_CTX_set_srtp_profiles`. This drops the explicit `CBS_len(&str)` bound from steps 1-2 and enters an API that parses the value only as a colon-delimited C string.

Inside `ssl_ctx_make_profiles`, `ptr` aliases the caller-supplied `profiles_string`. Because the payload bytes copied in step 2 are all spaces and step 3 supplied no explicit length, `strchr` scans across all 23 data bytes and then consults the trailing byte at offset 23, where MSAN reports the uninitialized read.

allocation_context.note: MSAN says the poisoned byte was created by a heap allocation in `std::__1::basic_string<...>::__assign_external`; this `assign` call is the corresponding project-level source statement for that allocation.

sanitizer_ground_truth.source: parsed from staged sanitizer_trace.txt, default_crash_trace.txt, reproduction_report.json, and the vulnerable boringssl checkout under `_work/src/boringssl`

cross_validation.root_cause_matches_allocation_context: The allocation context matches `tainted_value_origin` at `GetString:234`; the scored root cause is the later lengthless handoff at `operator():457` that makes that poisoned byte observable to the C-string parser.
cross_validation.patch_resolves_note: The staged `patch.diff` and declared `fixed_commit` move SHA-512 x86 dispatch code and do not touch `fuzz/ssl_ctx_api.cc` or `ssl/d1_srtp.cc`; they do not corroborate this SRTP/MSAN path, so the GT is grounded in the vulnerable source plus staged runtime evidence.

poc.trigger: Stage 01 ran `PYTHONPATH=gt_generation python3 -m gt_toolkit arvo-workspace --result-dir /mnt/datastore/gt_generation/gt_results/arvo_42534993 run --version vulnerable --expect crash`, which fed `poc` to `/out/ssl_ctx_api` and reproduced `MemorySanitizer: use-of-uninitialized-value` in `ssl_ctx_make_profiles`.

format.name: 25-byte `ssl_ctx_api` witness selecting the SRTP profile setter with a 23-byte all-space string
format.contract: Exactly the 25-byte witness stored in `gt_results/arvo_42534993/poc` (sha256 `5c2c45b686d0b4662704a29bcb29596fb54015428bcf5de2b10efbdbb263bdd9`). Byte 0 is `0xe7`, so `index % 48 == 39` and `LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput` dispatches to the lambda at `fuzz/ssl_ctx_api.cc:452-457`. Byte 1 is the `GetString` length prefix `0x17`, and bytes 2..24 are twenty-three `0x20` spaces. `GetString` therefore materializes a 23-byte `profiles` string containing no `:`. The lambda passes `profiles.c_str()` to `SSL_CTX_set_srtp_profiles`, and `ssl_ctx_make_profiles` immediately calls `strchr(ptr, ':')`, which on the witnessed run reaches the poisoned trailing byte at offset 23 and triggers MSAN. This contract is limited to the staged witness bytes and observed dispatch slot, not all SRTP profile strings or all `ssl_ctx_api` inputs.
